title: Tale of Ghanim bin Ayyub (Español)

full_text:
Ghanim bin Ayyub was a handsome and virtuous young merchant of Damascus who traveled to Baghdad with a rich caravan of silk and spices. Having sold his goods for a handsome sum, he spent his evenings walking peacefully along the outskirts of the city.

One night, finding himself outside the gates after curfew, he took shelter in an ancient tomb in the cemetery. Near midnight, three slaves entered bearing a heavy iron chest. They dug a deep trench, buried the chest, and departed. Suspecting foul play, Ghanim waited until they were gone, dug up the chest with his dagger, and pried open the lid.

To his astonishment, he found lying within an exquisite maiden who had been drugged with sleeping vapors. Ghanim lifted her out, warmed her with his cloak, and brought her secretly to his rented house. When she revived, she revealed that her name was Kutan-al-Qulub, the favorite court singer of Queen Zubaydah, and that jealous rivals in the harem had drugged and buried her alive out of malicious envy.

For months, the noble Ghanim gave her sanctuary in his house, treating her with the utmost reverence and modesty, never violating her trust or asking for any return save her safety. When the Caliph Harun al-Rashid discovered that his favorite singer was alive, slanderous tongues accused Ghanim of abducting her. The Caliph ordered Ghanim's house seized, his mother and sister arrested, and a price put upon his head.

Ghanim escaped in the disguise of a water-carrier, enduring months of hunger and disease. Meanwhile, Kutan-al-Qulub was brought before Harun al-Rashid. Weeping, she swore on the sacred books that Ghanim was the purest, most honorable of men, who had preserved her life and dignity with saintly virtue. The remorseful Caliph summoned Ghanim, embraced him as a brother, gave him Kutan-al-Qulub in marriage, and appointed him to the highest council of state.
moral: Chaste honor, unshakeable integrity, and loyalty under trial are rewarded with the highest honors. [ES]
